articles.title: Amnesia and déjà vu: how our AI agents failed after every restart (and how we fixed it)
articles.excerpt: An agent that crashes is annoying. An agent that crashes and comes back is where things get dangerous. When we started running our agents in production, we discovered that a restart could go wrong in…
articles.body: An agent that crashes is annoying. An agent that crashes and comes back is where things get dangerous. When we started running our agents in production, we discovered that a restart could go wrong in two completely opposite ways. Sometimes the agent came back with amnesia : it had forgotten everything, the conversation, the context, what it was in the middle of doing. And sometimes, when we tried to fix that by simply relaunching the work, it came back with déjà vu : it happily redid everything from the start, including the things it had already done in the real world. Like sending an email. Twice. This post is about both failures, why the obvious fixes don't work, and what we ended up building.
articles.author: Anis Meziani

articles.body: 2022년은 암호화폐 시장에 격동의 시기로 기록될 것이다. 이 해는 막대한 가격 하락과 더불어 여러 고위험 기관의 실패로 얼룩졌다. 그중에서도 싱가포르 기반의 유명 암호화폐 헤지펀드인 쓰리애로우즈캐피탈(Three Arrows Capital, 3AC)의 붕괴는 특히나 엄청난 지진과 같은 사건이었다. 한때 공격적인 투자 전략과 막대한 자본으로 찬사를 받던 3AC의 갑작스러운 파산은 디지털 자산 생태계 전반에 충격파를 던졌다. 이는 이전 강세장 동안 가려져 있던 깊이 뿌리박힌 시스템적 취약점을 여실히 드러내는 계기가 되었다. 수 주(Su Zhu)와 카일 데이비스(Kyle Davies)가 공동 설립한 3AC는 수십억 달러 규모의 자산을 운용하며 중앙화 금융(CeFi)과 탈중앙화 금융(DeFi) 양쪽에서 다양한 정교한 거래 및 투자 활동에 참여했다. 테라-루나(Terra-Luna) 생태계의 비극적인 붕괴와 거시경제적 역풍 등 여러 요인이 복합적으로 작용해 발생한 이들의 몰락은 결코 고립된 사건이 아니었다. 오히려 3AC의 파산은 강력한 촉매제 역할을 하며 연쇄적인 파산, 유동성 위기, 그리고 광범위한 전염을 촉발했다. 이는 수많은 다른 암호화폐 대출 플랫폼, 거래소, 투자 회사에 직접적인 영향을 미쳤다. 이 글에서는 3AC 붕괴의 복잡한 메커니즘을 깊이 파고들어 기술적, 재정적 여파를 분석하고, 구체적인 현실 속 전염 사례들을 살펴볼 것이다. 나아가 이러한 복잡한 사건을 이해하는 데 따르는 본질적인 한계를 논하며, 궁극적으로 디지털 자산 산업이 나아가야 할 방향과 얻은 교훈에 대한 전문가적 결론을 도출하고자 한다.
articles.author: Juno Kim

articles.title: Give your agent an agenda
articles.excerpt: I'm gonna go out on a limb and say you've probably used an AI agent before. I'm gonna go out on an even further limb and say you've probably built an AI agent before. When building agents that interac…
articles.body: I'm gonna go out on a limb and say you've probably used an AI agent before. I'm gonna go out on an even further limb and say you've probably built an AI agent before. When building agents that interact with humans, we often put a decent amount of effort into designing a character profile for them. Things like a name, tone, opinions, funny sayings to tack on to the end of sentences, all go into building the facade of a personality. Memory is in the list too, so the agent knows what happened yesterday. There's a surprising amount to all of it, including the science that goes into which memories to retrieve , but when it comes down to it, a lot of it is just messing around with a prompt. And every piece of it describes who the agent is or what already happened to it.

articles.title: Beyond Unit Tests: How to Test and Evaluate LLM Applications
articles.excerpt: Beyond Unit Tests: How to Test and Evaluate LLM Applications Imagine deploying an AI-powered chatbot. Your API returns 200 OK, all your unit tests pass, and the application responds within an acceptab…
articles.body: Beyond Unit Tests: How to Test and Evaluate LLM Applications Imagine deploying an AI-powered chatbot. Your API returns 200 OK , all your unit tests pass, and the application responds within an acceptable time. But there is one problem: the answer is wrong. The chatbot confidently provides an incorrect refund policy, invents a step that does not exist in the documentation, or answers a question that it does not have enough information to answer. From a traditional software testing perspective, everything looks fine. From the user's perspective, the application has failed. This is one of the biggest challenges when building applications powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Unlike traditional functions, LLMs can generate different responses to the same input.

articles.title: How to write a change order that customers actually sign
articles.excerpt: Every contractor has lived this: the job is half done, the customer says "while you're at it, can you also...", you say sure, and three weeks later you are arguing about a bill nobody agreed to in wri…
articles.body: Every contractor has lived this: the job is half done, the customer says "while you're at it, can you also...", you say sure, and three weeks later you are arguing about a bill nobody agreed to in writing. A change order fixes that. It is a short written record that the scope or price changed, and that the customer said yes. Here is how to do it well without turning it into paperwork. What a change order must contain What changed. One or two plain sentences. "Add two outlets on the east wall of the kitchen." What it costs. A number, not "a few hundred." Split labor and materials if you can. What it does to the schedule. "Adds one day." Even "no change" is worth writing. A reference to the original job. Quote number, address, or date, so it can be matched later. A yes from the customer.

articles.title: A tool call that gets cut off is four different failures, and only one of them is a timeout
articles.excerpt: A tool call that gets cut off is four different failures, and only one of them is a timeout Every agent framework has a number it will not let a tool call exceed. When a long call hits it, the framewo…
articles.body: A tool call that gets cut off is four different failures, and only one of them is a timeout Every agent framework has a number it will not let a tool call exceed. When a long call hits it, the framework reports one word — timeout — and the agent does one thing: call again . If the tool was a paid, non-idempotent call, that is the worst possible response, because the first call usually still finished. I maintain a decision endpoint that takes 180–300 seconds by design. It is a long call on purpose, and no argument in the tool schema makes it shorter: the limit lives in the client, not in the call. So I have watched the same failure arrive in four different shapes, and I collected the documented client behaviour for each.

articles.title: Designing Account Holds for Chargebacks
articles.excerpt: A State Machine for Digital Goods When a bank reverses a payment for a digital purchase, your system has to decide what happens to the account that made it. Most platforms treat that as a binary choic…
articles.body: A State Machine for Digital Goods When a bank reverses a payment for a digital purchase, your system has to decide what happens to the account that made it. Most platforms treat that as a binary choice: do nothing, or lock the account. Sony's handling on PlayStation Network is a well-known example of the second option. A reversed PlayStation Store charge suspends the account, the player sees error WS-37368-7 at sign-in, and access comes back once the debt is repaid. The policy, and how players have reacted to it, is covered in PlayStation Chargebacks: Sony's Chargeback Policy & the Hard Choices Behind the Ruleset . The interesting engineering problem is the one that article raises near the end. A single dispute event can come from three very different customers.

articles.body: In a milestone achievement, NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has broken the record for most miles driven on a world beyond Earth. On Oct. 11, Perseverance hit 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) traveled on Mars, breaking the record previously held by NASA's Opportunity rover which went 28.06 miles (45.16 km). It took Oppy 14 years to cover all that ground; Perseverance, by contrast, has been on Mars for just 5.5 years. The new record is far from the end of Perseverance's journey, however; the mission team thinks the rover could eventually more than double the distance it's already traveled. "Our original design was only planned to last for [about] 20 kilometers of driving," Mark Maimone, a rover driver at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, told Space.com .

What is it? Menon's photo reveals spectacular pink, purple and red auroras glowing in Earth's upper atmosphere above a sparse dappling of city lights, subtly blurred by the motion of the orbital spacecraft over the course of the exposure. Bright stars glimmer between the solar panels and outer hulls of the ISS and visiting spacecraft, painted purple by the auroral display. articles.title: The great Halley's Comet disappointment of 1986 — and the discoveries that changed astronomy forever
articles.excerpt: What disappointed skywatchers in 1986 became a scientific triumph, as an international fleet of spacecraft revealed the secrets of the world's most famous comet.
articles.body: This year, 2026, marks the 40th anniversary of the most recent appearance of Halley's Comet, the most famous comet in the solar system. Roughly every 76 years, Halley punctuates history like an exclamation mark in the night sky. As writer Guy Ottewell has said, it is the "wildest of the tame comets." It is a tame comet because it can be anticipated. It is wild because it is still fresh and bright; the brightest of all the recurring comets. It is the only one that periodically becomes conspicuous to the naked eye. Halley through history Before 1986, Halley had been seen and recorded on 29 occasions. In A.D. 66, observers described it as a sword in the skies above Jerusalem.
